case_title: Vijendra Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: accused's family was in enmity with the victim's uncle (PW-1) over a earlier murder case; victim was PW-1's nephew and all belonged to the same village
weapon: Gun/pistol (fatal gunshot); co-accused carried ballam and lathi
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (PWs 1-3), medical evidence (post-mortem), recovery of cartridges from spot, investigation documents (panchanama, sketch map)
aggravating_circumstances: Accused went armed with lathi/ballam alongside co-accused armed with gun; murder by gunshot
mitigating_circumstances: Appellant Vijendra was a juvenile (16 years 3 months 10 days) on the date of offence
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC; rigorous imprisonment for life
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and life sentence affirmed
neutral_facts: The victim, a student, stayed overnight in a shed at a tube-well in a field, where electric light was available for his studies. At about 7.30 p.m., two relatives of the victim, carrying meals for him, met a third villager who wanted to irrigate his fields, and the three walked to the tube-well together. Near the tube-well they heard the sound of a gunshot from inside the shed. They hurried to the spot and saw four men come out of the shed. Two carried pistols, one carried a ballam and one carried a lathi. On seeing the witnesses, the men ran away. The witnesses found the victim lying dead in a pool of blood. They identified the men by an electric bulb on the shed roof and by torchlight. A report was prepared on the spot with the help of the victim's uncle and an FIR was lodged at the police station the same night. Investigators recorded witness statements, prepared a panchanama and sketch map, and collected blood-stained and unstained earth and two cartridges from the spot. The post-mortem found eight gunshot entry wounds on the right side of the neck and no blackening or scorching around the wound. The doctor opined that death was caused by gunshot injury. There was enmity between the accused's family and the victim's uncle's family arising from an earlier murder case in which the uncle had faced prosecution.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from gunshot injuries; eight entry wounds on right side of neck
premeditation_planning: No premeditation or pre-arranged plan found; court held common intention may be formed on the spot, and the group's intention to go to the shed was established
motive: Alleged: revenge over the earlier murder case in which the victim's uncle had faced prosecution; the court noted that PWs 1-3 deposed about this previous enmity
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of PWs 1-3 (identification, weapons carried, presence at spot, victim lying in blood); cartridges recovered from spot; doctor's evidence that death was from gunshot injury
witness_credibility: PWs 1-3 found trustworthy and reliable; related witnesses not treated as interested; PW-3 not discredited as a chance witness; cross-examination elicited nothing to discredit them
post_offence_conduct: Accused fled the scene on being seen; all accused except Dhani Ram later surrendered before the Court; Dhani Ram was arrested later
custody_duration: Vijendra remained in custody beyond the maximum juvenile confinement period; exact duration not stated
trial_duration: offence: 26.03.1979; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 13.05.2009; Supreme Court: 04.01.2017
legal_representation: Accused: Mukesh K. Giri, Advocate. State: R. K. Dash, Senior Advocate, with Ms. Archana Singh and others
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; charge sheet filed; trial held and completed in Sessions Court
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC, life imprisonment. High Court: appeals dismissed (appeal abated for Dhani Ram, who died). Supreme Court: Mahendra's appeal dismissed; Vijendra's conviction sustained but released as juvenile
prosecution_argument: Conviction under s.34 supported; non-examination of witnesses does not affect the prosecution case; Vijendra's juvenility conceded and compensation suggested
defence_argument: No common intention or meeting of minds; witnesses interested and contradictory; PW-3 a chance witness; non-examination of independent witnesses; no lathi/ballam injury and medical evidence of no scorching; Vijendra a juvenile
legal_principle_applied: Section 34 applies on facts; common intention may form on the spot; carrying weapons, arriving together, entering the shed and the killing attract constructive liability; interested-witness and non-examination tests applied
precedent_relied_upon: Pandurang v. State of Hyderabad (AIR 1955 SC 216); Mohan Singh v. State of Punjab (AIR 1963 SC 174); Harshadsingh Pahelvansingh Thakore v. State of Gujarat (1976) 4 SCC 640; Suresh Sakharam Nangare (2012) 9 SCC 249; Jai Bhagwan (1999) 3 SCC 102; Hari Obula Reddy (1981) 3 SCC 675; Rana Pratap (1983) 3 SCC 327; Hari Ram (2009) 13 SCC 211
judicial_mitigating_factors: Juvenility of Vijendra (16 years 3 months 10 days at offence) and his prolonged custody beyond the juvenile confinement maximum
other_sentence_order: Vijendra released from custody forthwith as a juvenile; Criminal Appeal No. 1452 of 2010 dismissed; Criminal Appeal No. 1448 of 2010 disposed of
